title: Instant Pot 9-in-1 Duo Plus 5.7L Electric Pressure Cooker $109.16 (RRP $159) Delivered @ Amazon AU (Excl. NT)
body:
Deal: Instant Pot 9-in-1 Duo Plus 5.7L Electric Pressure Cooker $109.16 (RRP $159) Delivered @ Amazon AU (Excl. NT)

[poxy001] Just cooked this in it. Very nice.
https://www.seriouseats.com/quick-and-easy-pressure-cooker-c…
[donman92] Anyone have any issues with spag bowl sticking after slow cooking for a few hours?
[poxy001] Add more water so its just over the pasta, add oil and salt. Works beautifully.
[EnALup] Do you buy steamer basket separate to steam veggies in it ? If yes, can you sharewaht you bought ?
[mfu] Not veggies, but I steam dumpling or dimsims. I use bamboo steamer, usually any asian groceries has it. Kmart also has bamboo steamer but either too large or too small.
[webmonkey] I reckon the 8L pot is more practical. After you've taken into account the max fill line you're filling about 3/4 of the volume.
[CocaKoala] I reckon the 8L pot is more practical.
That depends on how much you would want to cook in one go, and I respect that some families will be making much larger portions regularly.
After you've taken into account the max fill line you're filling about 3/4 of the volume.
Yeah mate, that's because of physics. Food expands when cooked, so the 3/4 of the volume has become 4/4 after cooking and the pot is full. Filling it up over that line is not meaningful when you think about it, and I would hazard a guess that the 8L cooker will also have its max fill line in its pot.
That said, I will not suggest the 8L at its current selling price and would rather wait for a deal on it. The 5.7L though is at an excellent price point now.
[racer1234] Anyone know how hard these are to clean?
[CocaKoala] The inner bowl is stainless steel which can be easily hand washed (I find it too big to put into the dishwasher for my taste). That said, the lid as well as the bowl are dishwasher safe. It can't get easier than that to clean tbh.
[racer1234] I found some instructions for deep cleaning the lid, which apparently has to be done every 2-3 uses. Sounded very fiddly. Any experience with this?
[CocaKoala] I find it simple enough, but I do clean it right after preparing something like a big meal so perhaps that makes it easy for me. If you leave it for days on end that might then be harder I suppose.
[Magpye] The lid itself is easy enough to clean, it's the silicon seal band that needs to be sterilised. It absorbs smells from the food, so simply swap it out (you get a spare) and soak it overnight.
You can always buy more of them, if you need to rotate them out more often, but it's not a requirement.
[Geewhizz] @Magpye: Just pop the seal oit in the sin for a bit to get rid of any smells.
[Magpye] @Geewhizz: I've found any pressure cooked stews with fish based sauces (worcestershire sauce) would resist a casual soak, but awesome if that works for you.
[Jackson] @Magpye: Never done this with my pressure cooker despite using for many years and never had an issue
[Jackson] I finally get to have a 5.7L, if only I could drive it
[Jackson] I had a 3.8, was decent but the maintenance was a lot for a young bloke
[Jewdas90] Don't think maintenance is the biggest issue these days XD
[CocaKoala] I use it to cook stews, soups, differnt kinds of rice, porridge, cereals, lentils and hard to cook pulses ( kidney beans, chickpeas, navy beans, etc). Another reason I use regularly is to make greek yoghurt🤌
